text: Why does the choice of programming language change K(s) only by an additive constant?
choices: Because all Turing-complete languages have the same number of instructions.
Because compression ratios are language-independent by the source coding theorem.
Because K is defined as the minimum over all languages, so no single language matters.
An interpreter for one language can be written in another, so any program can be converted by prepending a fixed-length interpreter.
explanation: The constant depends on the two languages and not on the string, so for long strings the choice is negligible and K is well defined up to an additive constant. That is the invariance theorem, and it is Chapter 25 used as a proof technique: the reason languages are interchangeable up to a constant is that you can write one inside another, which you have done.
